description: To be read on Sunday next

participation.context: Read the sheet and did not add a word.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Has the precept by heart by supper. She does not speak in this stretch.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

story.body: You read the clerk's sheet. The order is no blue starch in ruffs, from Crosby Place, to be read on Sunday next.

title: Read the precept before supper

participation.context: Asked the question about collars, and kept the loaf at a finger and a half.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Had the precept by heart, gave the two sentences, and allowed the washing.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Sat still, owned the one band, and took leave to wash it white.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

relations.note: she gives leave to wash the band white
relations.quote: Then you may wash it white.

story.body: You asked about the dearth and the collars. Mistress Ansell sided with the Mayor on ruffs and let Alse wash the one blue band. The loaf stayed a finger and a half short. The clerk was not at the table.

relations.note: she gives leave to wash the band white
relations.quote: Then you may wash it white.

title: Heard the blue-starch precept and that Alse may wash the band white
